title: Unary division by a natural number
statement: Let $f$ be a function from binary words to natural numbers whose unary representation is polynomial-time computable. For every natural number $k$, the function that maps $x$ to the unary representation of $�f(x)/k�$ is polynomial-time computable, where division is natural-number division and in particular $f(x)/0=0$.
hypotheses_covered: The unary representation of $f(x)$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If a unary value is polynomial-time computable, then for every fixed constant $k$ the unary word of its quotient by $k$ is polynomial-time computable: a finite-control counter emits one bit per completed block, and division by zero yields the empty word.
